public_payload.normalized_proposition: Highway miles are the easy part of the promised intervention-free LA-to-NYC drive, and nobody even pretends anymore to be close to making such a drive off the Interstate.

statement.excerpt: (And highways miles are the easy part; nobody even pretends anymore to be close to doing that off the Interstate).

from_speaker: highways miles are the easy part
an intervention-free drive, without human assistance, from LA to NYC
our_interpretation: 'Doing that' retains the preceding sentence's entire task: an intervention-free LA-to-NYC drive without human assistance, using a route off the Interstate.
'The easy part' ordinarily means highway driving presents less autonomous-driving difficulty than the off-Interstate portions of that task; it does not mean highway driving is risk-free.
'Nobody even pretends' concerns public claims of being near that capability, rather than whether the capability was actually achieved.

The target is the public state of claims and technical capability as of the post on 2023-01-18. This subject has no fixed reporting quarter; the latest reportable state is the information publicly current at posting.
No numerical definition of 'close' is added. Clear claims of imminent readiness would qualify; generic ambitions or local driverless services would not.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence must establish both that highway driving was the comparatively easier part of this cross-country task and that a sufficiently comprehensive contemporaneous record contained no public claim of nearing an intervention-free LA-to-NYC drive off the Interstate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A contemporaneously current public statement clearly claiming near readiness for that specific off-Interstate cross-country task would contradict the second part. Comparable technical evidence showing highway driving was not the easier part would contradict the first. Local autonomy alone would not do either.
